I enjoy reading Ron Unz's deep-dives on race issues, and often find them illuminating, but you have to take him with a grain of salt. He is a natural contrarian at heart, and is not above using statistics to obscure reality when it suits him.

His basic argument is: Hispanics in the U.S. show an incarceration rate that is about 2.5x the incarceration rate for whites, but crime is a young man's game, and the incarceration rate for whites overall is deceptively low because the U.S. is filled with a lot of old white people.

So if you want a real comparison of criminality, you have to compare like by like: the incarceration rate of young white males to the incarceration rate of young Hispanic males. And if you do that (in this very specific way that ignores a lot of data) they're about the same.

What Unz leaves out is that prison itself is mostly a first world problem. If you are criminally-minded--that is, if you are prone to raping, assaulting, stabbing, murdering, threatening, pimping, selling illegal drugs, and so on--you do not need to come to the U.S. to do these things, and in fact, you significantly increase your likelihood of incarceration by doing so. Most U.S. cities simply will not put up with the kind of crime rates you see in Latin countries. For a clearer picture of the criminal tendencies of Hispanic populations, the natural place to look is in majority Hispanic countries. And the picture we see is not a pretty one.

Crime is now so rampant in Mexico, for example, that even resort towns which traditionally cater to the white tourist trade (and thus have a greater interest in maintaining law and order than non-resort towns) are becoming overwhelmed with violence and corruption. The Mexican government had to literally disband the entire police force in Acapulco just last week because it was hopelessly corrupt and in the covert employ of the drug cartels:

Acapulco, once one of the country’s preeminent tourist hotspots famous as a favorite haunt among movie stars in the 1960s, has turned into one of Mexico’s most dangerous cities with dead bodies being hung from bridges and human heads being left in coolers outside city hall.

In Acapulco alone, the homicide rate last year was 103 per 100,000 habitants – one of the highest in Mexico and the world. The situation is so dire that in May, clowns marched demanding an end to the city’s crime wave, saying they were losing business because residents no longer threw parties out of fear of becoming targets, the BBC reported.

(Just by way of comparison, the murder rate in Chicago, currently experiencing an explosion of violent crime? About 30 per 100,000 as of 2016. Less than a third of Acapulco's.)

Beyond this, Unz's argument basically comes down to, "If things wasn't the way they are, they wouldn't be the way they is." Yes, if we lived in a country where the demographics of Hispanic immigrants had just as many 40+ people in them as our existing white demographics do, then Hispanic incarceration rates might look (a little) more like white incarceration rates. But we don't, so they don't. And I don't want to get too deep into r/K selection theory, but there are lots of reasons why Latin populations skew much younger (and therefore, by Unz's own arguments, more criminally-inclined) than European nations. The median age in Mexico is 28. The median age in the U.S. is 38.

To the extent Unz's argument has some validity, it's because many Hispanics who come to the U.S. actually do come to escape the conditions in their home nations, and not to spread them.
